title: Investigative and Interviewing Skills for Supervisors
summary: An eight-module practical programme on planning and conducting supervisory interviews and turning interview evidence into sound findings.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors to plan and conduct effective interviews with directors, senior managers and control functions, test what they hear against the evidence, and turn interview evidence into sound supervisory findings.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a structured, practical approach to investigative interviewing in on-site inspections, reviews and governance assessments. Participants leave able to plan an interview, question with purpose, recognise evasion, record reliable evidence and draw defensible conclusions, drawing on a course already delivered to a supervisory authority.
sections.What It Covers: The purpose and mindset of supervisory interviews, a PEACE-style interview structure, planning and preparation, open, probing and funnel questioning, active listening and reading evasion, document-based questioning and recording evidence, interviewing boards and control functions, difficult interviewees, and moving from interview to finding.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors who conduct on-site visits, thematic reviews and governance assessments
Staff assessing fitness and propriety of directors and senior managers, including authorisation teams
Team leaders who plan inspections and review interview evidence before findings are issued
Learning Objectives: Explain the purpose of supervisory interviews and the mindset they require
Plan an interview with clear objectives, lines of enquiry and supporting documents
Apply open, probing and funnel questioning within a structured interview model
Evaluate the credibility, consistency and reliability of responses, including evasion
Manage difficult, evasive or defensive interviewees while keeping control of the interview
Record interview evidence accurately and link it to supervisory findings and action
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with questioning exercises, case studies and a closing role-play workshop, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's inspection approach.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of on-site inspections or firm engagement is helpful. No prior interview training is required.
Core Reading: Rebecca Milne and Ray Bull, Investigative Interviewing: Psychology and Practice (1999)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)

modules.title: The Supervisory Interview: Purpose and Mindset
modules.summary: Why supervisors interview, how supervisory interviews differ from enforcement interviews and recruitment interviews, and how mindset shapes what the interviewer hears.
objectives: Explain the role of interviews in risk assessment, inspections and governance reviews
Distinguish supervisory from enforcement interviews and their evidential standards
Recognise how assumptions and mindset affect an interview
syllabus: Interviews in the supervisory cycle: inspections, reviews and fitness and propriety
Supervisory versus enforcement interviews: purpose, powers and safeguards
Introducing a PEACE-style structure for supervisory interviews
The right supervisory perspective: curious, sceptical and fair

modules.title: Planning and Preparing the Interview
modules.summary: How to set objectives, research the interviewee and the firm, select documents, build lines of enquiry and agree roles within the interview team.
objectives: Define interview objectives linked to the supervisory risk assessment
Prepare an interview plan with lines of enquiry and supporting evidence
Organise the interview team, logistics and introductions
syllabus: Setting objectives and identifying the right interviewees
Desk research: board papers, management information and prior findings
Building the interview plan and question map
Roles: lead questioner, note-taker and observer

modules.title: Questioning Techniques: Open, Probing and Funnel
modules.summary: The question types that elicit full and accurate accounts, how to sequence them using the funnel technique, and the questioning habits that undermine an interview.
objectives: Apply open, probing and closed questions for the right purpose
Use the funnel technique to move from broad accounts to specific facts
Avoid leading, multiple and assumptive questions
syllabus: Open questions to obtain a free account
Probing and clarifying questions to test detail and gaps
Funnel sequencing: from general to specific to confirmation
Exercise: rewriting weak questions into effective ones

modules.title: Active Listening, Credibility and Reading Evasion
modules.summary: How to listen for what is said and not said, assess the credibility and consistency of answers, and recognise and respond to evasion, deflection and rehearsed responses.
objectives: Apply active listening and summarising techniques during an interview
Evaluate the consistency and plausibility of responses against other evidence
Recognise verbal signs of evasion and follow them up
syllabus: Active listening: silence, summarising and reflecting back
Testing accounts for consistency, plausibility and corroboration
Evasion patterns: deflection, generalisation, scripted and partial answers
Limits of non-verbal cues and avoiding false conclusions

modules.title: Document-Based Questioning and Recording Evidence
modules.summary: How to use board papers, policies, minutes and data to question interviewees effectively, and how to record interview evidence so it is accurate, complete and usable later.
objectives: Use documents to test accounts and confront inconsistencies
Record interview evidence accurately and contemporaneously
Assess when an interview record must meet a higher evidential standard
syllabus: Selecting and sequencing documents for disclosure in the interview
Putting inconsistencies to the interviewee fairly
Note-taking, recordings, transcripts and agreed notes
Storing, sharing and relying on interview records

modules.title: Interviewing Boards, Senior Managers and Control Functions
modules.summary: How to tailor interviews to chairs, non-executives, chief executives and heads of risk, compliance and internal audit, and what each interview should reveal about governance and control.
objectives: Tailor questioning to the role and accountabilities of the interviewee
Assess board challenge, executive accountability and control function independence
Identify governance red flags from interview evidence
syllabus: Interviewing chairs and non-executive directors on challenge and oversight
Interviewing executives on strategy, risk and accountability
Interviewing heads of risk, compliance and internal audit on independence and resources
Governance red flags: dominant individuals, weak challenge and information gaps

modules.title: Managing Difficult Interviews
modules.summary: Techniques for handling defensive, hostile, evasive or over-talkative interviewees, the involvement of legal advisers, and keeping control of the interview without compromising fairness.
objectives: Apply techniques to manage defensive, hostile and evasive interviewees
Maintain control and fairness when advisers or colleagues intervene
Decide when to pause, re-plan or escalate an interview
syllabus: Types of difficult interviewee and why they behave as they do
De-escalation, re-framing and returning to the question
Legal advisers, compliance chaperones and interruptions
When to stop, re-plan or escalate

modules.title: From Interview to Finding: Role-Play Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a full simulated interview based on a case study, followed by evaluation of the evidence and drafting of supervisory conclusions and next steps.
objectives: Conduct a complete interview using the techniques covered in the programme
Evaluate interview evidence alongside documents and data
Draw supervisory conclusions and link them to proportionate action
syllabus: Evaluating the interview: what was established and what remains open
Weighing interview evidence with documentary and data evidence
From evidence to finding, follow-up request or escalation
Workshop: role-play interview, debrief and draft findings

related.title: Supervisory Judgement and Professional Practice
related.summary: A ten-module programme on forming, documenting and defending supervisory judgements, and turning them into clear findings, letters and interventions.

related.title: Core Professional Skills for Regulatory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme building the core writing, analysis, meeting, challenge, presentation and data skills that regulatory staff need every day.

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Risk Governance Panels
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to a risk governance panel, using running case studies and role plays.

related.title: Foundations of Financial Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module induction for new regulatory staff covering why we regulate, the authority's powers, risk-based supervision and a first supervisory case.

related.title: How Financial Firms Work: Business Models and Financial Statements for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping supervisors understand how financial firms make money, read their accounts and identify capital, liquidity and business model risks.
